Hi Sam / Laura,

Thanks again for taking the time today — appreciated the thoughtful questions. Quick recap from our discovery call and proposed next steps focused on logging controls and redaction: 

Call recap:
- Primary concern: ensure request/response logs and headers do not leak PII or sensitive identifiers (account IDs, trace IDs, auth tokens).
- FinTechCo requirements: configurable redaction, short retention windows for request/response payloads, option to disable persistent logging for sensitive routes, and data residency in the US (with EU option for specific projects).
- Compliance: you mentioned SOC 2 + PCI scoping for parts of this workload; want to confirm we can meet evidence/controls asked by your security team.

What Redwood can do (high level):
- Configurable redaction profiles by route (regex & token-level rules), header masking, and automatic removal of common PII patterns.
- Retention controls: per-customer/per-route retention (24h, 7d, 90d), plus auto-expunge.
- Operational modes: default telemetry-only logging (no request/response bodies) or enabled request/response logging with redaction. Dedicated/private customers can opt into no-logging or region-locked storage.

Open questions for FinTechCo (so we can prepare a targeted deep-dive):
1) Examples of the PII/identifiers you need redacted (e.g., SSNs, account numbers, card fragments, internal trace IDs).
2) Which routes are considered sensitive (payment processing, KYC intake, support channels)?
3) Retention policy target for request/response payloads and audit logs.

Proposed next steps:
- I'll share a short runbook that outlines our redaction controls and options (attached).
- Technical deep-dive with our security/SE (Dylan + Connor) — proposed Tue 16 Feb 2027, 10:00am PST (I’ll include a Calendly link below).
- If possible, please share any sample payloads or a checklist from your security team so we can prepare concrete examples.

Attached: redwood-logging-controls.pdf (contains redaction profiles, retention options, and example configs).

Thanks — talk soon.

Best,

1) Do you ever store full request/response bodies by default? If so, how long and where (region)?
2) For streaming cases (websocket/streaming responses), can Redwood avoid persisting the content entirely while still supporting streaming to clients?

5) Attachments: will attachments ever be stored by Redwood (we have file uploads containing documents with PII)?

Hi Sam — quick technical answers ahead of tomorrow’s deep-dive (adding a few actionable notes you can share with your security team).

1) Default logging behavior:
- By default Redwood captures metadata (timestamps, model id, route, latency, success/failure codes) for observability. Full request/response bodies are NOT persisted by default in the hosted plan unless request/response logging is explicitly enabled for a route.

2) Streaming support without persistence:
- Yes — we support ephemeral streaming mode: tokens are proxied to the client and not persisted. This is available in both hosted and dedicated flows; dedicated/private deployments can enforce ephemeral-only at the network/proxy layer.

3) Headers & trace IDs:
- We have header masking rules that allow you to redact specific header keys (Authorization, Cookie, X-User-Id, etc.).
- For trace IDs we offer two options: (a) hash/anonymize the trace ID before storage (keeping correlation within logs for a tenant), or (b) strip trace IDs from persisted logs but emit ephemeral correlation IDs to the live trace pipeline. Hashing uses a tenant-scoped salt so IDs are non-reversible across tenants.

4) Redaction rules & management:
- Redaction profiles are configurable per-route and per-tenant. Profiles support regex rules, token classification (PII types), and allow exceptions for approved fields.
- Rules can be managed via our Management API (we’ll include API examples in the attached runbook).

5) Attachments and file uploads:
- Attachments are not persisted by default. If a customer enables attachment capture, we store them in the region you select with retention policy applied. For sensitive uploads we recommend: disable capture, or store only metadata (filename, mime-type) and route files to your own S3 bucket via our secure transfer integration.

6) Retention & auto-expunge:
- Retention windows are tenant-configurable; typical presets are 24h, 7d, 90d. Auto-expunge runs nightly; deletions are logged to an audit trail (audit logs can be configured to retain only non-PII metadata).

7) Dedicated/Private options:
- For Dedicated (reserved capacity) and Private deployments we support region-locked storage and an option to disable request/response logging entirely at the control plane level. That path is recommended for PCI-scoped workloads.

Attached I’ve added a short runbook with example Management API calls and sample redaction regexes (see redwood-logging-controls.pdf). I’ll bring examples to the call.

If useful, we can also provide a short demo showing: enabling a redaction profile, sending a sample request with a mocked SSN, and showing what’s retained in the logs.
